title: Did The Drug War Claim Another 3,056 Casualties On 9-11? Ariana Huffington’s Extraordinary Indictment.

content_html_sanitized:
Posted June 4, 2002
(MarijuanaNews note: The evidence mounts daily of a level of governmental incompetence that would result in criminal negligence charges in the private sector. Nonetheless, September 11 is being cynically used by the Bush Administration -- and by the drug warriors in particular - to increase the power of those who so outrageously failed to protect the American people from a clear and present danger.

However, there are now investigations underway, and this is a story that will not go away. It cannot be overshadowed by any other story, but will the really important, fundamental questions be asked? A new column by Ariana Huffington does just that.

If there is a meeting point between libertarians, conservatives and even liberals and on leftward, it should be Macaulay’s observation that governments which try to do more than they should, end by doing less than they ought.

The fact is that even the richest societies have finite resources. Not only is there insufficient money to do everything that everyone would like to do, there is far too little human talent. That is certainly true in law enforcement and in espionage, but there are very few areas of human endeavor in which there is greater need for more talented individuals. And there is no area of human endeavor where there is a greater need for the highest standards and more danger to those standards. It is very difficult for humans not to become like those whom they are fighting.

Sadly, there is also no other area of human endeavor in which current conditions are such that highly qualified people are more likely to be driven away than drawn in. One reason for that problem is that law enforcement and espionage are also similar in having substantial ideological characteristics. That is necessary in order to identify the " bad guys. "

Especially in DEAland, but also in Canada and the UK, prohibitionism is the dominant ideology amongst the politicized law enforcement leadership and anyone is perceived as a " legalizer " is unwelcome. That sets their priorities.

It is essential that the military be rescued from this political contamination. Involving the military in the drug war is a very dangerous business.

It is now recognized that there is a great need for added law enforcement and espionage capabilities. Perhaps, but we already have massive resources in these fields, and where were they when we really needed them?

Ariana Huffington says they were looking in the wrong places for the wrong people and the wrong things. Huffington is certainly one of the most independent thinkers. She does not fit into a neat ideological category, but she is quite brilliant, even when I disagree with her. And I certainly don’t disagree with what she is saying here.

As the old saying goes, read it and weep.
